data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 result is an artifact of masking, not of genuine test strength: mutations no guard catches are reported as caught because the installation ritual's failure registry is itself the oracle, so the test constrains its subject only when the subject participates in the ritual's masking.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If an independent oracle (not the installation registry) confirms the 3 survivors are genuinely uncaught, then masking is not the explanation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the compile.py loss can be reproduced without the installation ritual, then the masking is not installation-specific.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 to 6/7 spread is monotonic in module size, then the masking is uniform, not selective.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the same mutations under a different test harness produce the same 3-of-26, then the constraint is in the code, not the ritual.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The record notes that in the 59/3 case the error was masking: mutations no guard catches were reported as caught. This implies a self-referential oracle: the test's verdict is derived from the registry of shown failures, not from an independent description of correct behavior. Under this regime, a test constrains when it forces the subject into a shape that the registry already anticipates; it merely describes when the subject falls outside the registry's vocabulary. The 1/9 compile.py mutation loss is a masking failure at the build stage, while the 3/26 distribution is the subset of mutations that happen to align with the registry's blind spots.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
